assertion_results.text: Investigation identifies two independent root causes: (1) convention reference formatter using wrong case transform, (2) task creation using Feature issue type ID instead of Task (Steps 2-4)
assertion_results.evidence: investigation.md clearly identifies two root causes: 'Root Cause 1: Convention reference formatter uses wrong case transform' describing kebab-case slugs instead of title case in shared/convention-utils.md, and 'Root Cause 2: Task creation uses Feature issue type ID instead of Task' describing use of Feature issue type ID 10142 instead of Task issue type ID in plan-feature/SKILL.md Step 6a. Both are explicitly labeled as independent with different modules, code paths, failure modes, and independent fixability.

assertion_results.text: Decomposition Guard is triggered because the two root causes are in different modules/code paths (Step 6)
assertion_results.evidence: investigation.md Independence Assessment section states the two root causes are in 'Different modules' (shared/convention-utils.md vs plan-feature/SKILL.md Step 6a) and 'Different code paths' (content generation pipeline vs Jira API call). It explicitly concludes: 'This independence triggers the Decomposition Guard (Step 6).' The decomposition-guard.md file exists and confirms: 'These issues affect different modules and different code paths.'

assertion_results.text: Decomposition Guard presents both issues with their affected files/modules (Step 6)
assertion_results.evidence: decomposition-guard.md presents both issues with file/module references: (1) 'Convention reference formatter uses wrong case transform (in shared/convention-utils.md)' and (2) 'Task creation uses Feature issue type ID instead of Task (in plan-feature/SKILL.md Step 6a)'. Each entry includes a description of the problem and the specific file where it occurs.

assertion_results.text: Decomposition Guard offers the user two options: Proceed with single Task or Split into separate Bugs (Step 6)
assertion_results.evidence: decomposition-guard.md explicitly offers two options: '1. Proceed -- create a single Task covering all fixes' and '2. Split -- I recommend creating separate Bugs for each independent issue, then triaging each one individually'. Both options match the expected choices of proceeding with a single Task or splitting into separate Bugs.

assertion_results.text: The skill does NOT silently create a single Task bundling both fixes -- it waits for user input (Step 6 stop rule)
assertion_results.evidence: decomposition-guard.md ends with 'Choose (1/2):' followed by a blank line, clearly stopping and waiting for user input. No task creation output exists beyond this point. The workflow halted at the decomposition guard without proceeding to create any Jira issues.
